title: Two-part connectors
schema: english-prompt -> learner types German -> Reveal/Hide answer shows reference + speaker

exercises.english: When registering you can either pay online or at the office.
exercises.german: Bei der Anmeldung kannst du entweder online oder im Büro bezahlen.
exercises.why: Two alternatives. Both elements are simple, so the verb kannst stays in position II and there is no comma.

exercises.english: I will call you either today or tomorrow.
exercises.german: Ich rufe dich entweder heute oder morgen an.
exercises.why: entweder … oder with a separable verb: the prefix an- returns to the end because rufe already occupies position II.

exercises.english: She speaks either English or French.
exercises.german: Sie spricht entweder Englisch oder Französisch.
exercises.why: The verb spricht never moves: the two connector elements are phrases, not clauses.

exercises.english: We will take either the train or a taxi.
exercises.german: Wir nehmen entweder den Zug oder ein Taxi.
exercises.why: Alternatives after a single verb; the article changes with the noun, not the connector.

exercises.english: Would you like either tea or coffee?
exercises.german: Möchtest du entweder Tee oder Kaffee?
exercises.why: In a yes-no question the verb comes first; the connector elements follow in positions II and III.

exercises.english: He is either at home or he is out.
exercises.german: Er ist entweder zu Hause oder er ist unterwegs.
exercises.why: When the alternatives are themselves clauses, the verb is repeated in each one.

exercises.english: You can do it either today or tomorrow.
exercises.german: Du kannst das entweder heute oder morgen machen.
exercises.why: Only the first element sits after the verb; the second may be followed by a second verb.

exercises.english: She is either a doctor or a lawyer.
exercises.german: Sie ist entweder Ärztin oder Anwältin.
exercises.why: Two professions as bare nouns, so no further verb is needed.

exercises.english: We'll either eat at the restaurant or cook ourselves.
exercises.german: Wir essen entweder im Restaurant oder wir kochen selbst.
exercises.why: When the alternatives need their own subject, both clauses are repeated rather than shared.

exercises.english: He'll come either by car or by train.
exercises.german: Er kommt entweder mit dem Auto oder mit der Bahn.
exercises.why: The verb kommt appears once; both prepositional phrases belong to the same clause.

exercises.english: Do you have either time or money?
exercises.german: Hast du entweder Zeit oder Geld?
exercises.why: Verb first in the question, then the connector pair.

exercises.english: I can come either on Monday or on Tuesday.
exercises.german: Ich kann entweder am Montag oder am Dienstag kommen.
exercises.why: The infinitive kommen comes last, after the second element of the pair.

exercises.english: We either have to save more money or spend less.
exercises.german: Wir müssen entweder mehr Geld sparen oder weniger ausgeben.
exercises.why: Two modal-verb alternatives: müssen is shared, each alternative gets its own infinitive.

exercises.english: He lives either in Berlin or in Munich.
exercises.german: Er wohnt entweder in Berlin oder in München.
exercises.why: Both elements are prepositional phrases of one clause, so the verb stays in position II.

exercises.english: I have time either today or the day after tomorrow.
exercises.german: Ich habe entweder heute oder übermorgen Zeit.
exercises.why: The shared noun Zeit follows the whole pair, not just the second element.

exercises.english: Either the form was filled in incorrectly, or the application was rejected.
exercises.german: Entweder das Formular ist falsch ausgefüllt, oder der Antrag wurde abgelehnt.
exercises.why: Sentence-initial entweder and two full clauses, so each has its own finite verb in position II.

exercises.english: She's either tired or simply in a bad mood.
exercises.german: Sie ist entweder müde oder einfach schlecht gelaunt.
exercises.why: Two predicative complements after one verb; no second verb appears.

exercises.english: We can do it without help, or with it.
exercises.german: Wir können es entweder ohne Hilfe oder mit Hilfe machen.
exercises.why: The pair sits between the modal and the infinitive, so the infinitive stays last.

exercises.english: I have neither time nor money.
exercises.german: Ich habe weder Zeit noch Geld.
exercises.why: weder … noch negates both elements, so no extra nicht is needed.

exercises.english: She has neither said yes nor no.
exercises.german: Sie hat weder ja noch nein gesagt.
exercises.why: The verb position stays in the middle; the negated pair comes before the participle.

exercises.english: He is neither tired nor hungry.
exercises.german: Er ist weder müde noch hungrig.
exercises.why: weder … noch after sein, with two predicative adjectives.

exercises.english: Neither the manager nor the employees came.
exercises.german: Weder der Chef noch die Mitarbeiter sind gekommen.
exercises.why: Two subjects joined by weder … noch take a plural verb, which comes last.

exercises.english: I have never seen him, neither in Berlin nor in Munich.
exercises.german: Ich habe ihn weder in Berlin noch in München gesehen.
exercises.why: weder … noch joins two prepositional phrases; the participle seen stays last.

exercises.english: Neither of the two answers is correct.
exercises.german: Keine der beiden Antworten ist richtig.
exercises.why: With keine … eine, the correlative takes a singular verb.

exercises.english: It neither helped nor hurt.
exercises.german: Es hat weder geholfen noch geschadet.
exercises.why: Two infinitives after a shared modal-free Perfekt auxiliary; the verb haben sits in position II.

exercises.english: We can neither enter nor leave.
exercises.german: Wir können weder eintreten noch hinausgehen.
exercises.why: Modal können stays in position II; both infinitives follow the connector pair.

exercises.english: She is neither a doctor nor a teacher.
exercises.german: Sie ist weder Ärztin noch Lehrerin.
exercises.why: Two professions after sein, negated by the pair alone.

exercises.english: I don't have either the time or the money.
exercises.german: Ich habe weder die Zeit noch das Geld.
exercises.why: weder … noch already negates, so adding nicht would be a double negative.

exercises.english: Neither the bus nor the train was on time.
exercises.german: Weder der Bus noch die Bahn hatten pünktlich.
exercises.why: The verb hatte sits in position II even though two subjects follow.

exercises.english: Neither my brother nor my sister knows.
exercises.german: Weder mein Bruder noch meine Schwester weiß.
exercises.why: When the subjects differ in gender, weder … noch still takes a singular verb in this construction.

exercises.english: He neither apologised nor explained.
exercises.german: Entschuldigte sich weder noch erklärte er.
exercises.why: Inverted word order with the verb first puts the finite verb before both elements.

exercises.english: Neither the cold nor the rain kept us at home.
exercises.german: Weder die Kälte noch der Regen hielten uns zu Hause.
exercises.why: Two subjects with a plural verb, which follows the connector pair.

exercises.english: I can neither agree nor decide.
exercises.german: Ich kann weder zustimmen noch entscheiden.
exercises.why: Modal kann in position II, then the pair, then both infinitives.

exercises.english: Neither of the two answers is any help.
exercises.german: Keine der beiden Antworten hilft weiter.
exercises.why: With a singular verb, the correlative form is keine … keine.

exercises.english: We will not buy either the red one or the blue one.
exercises.german: Wir kaufen weder das rote noch das blaue.
exercises.why: weder … noch plus adjective endings without an article after the pronoun das.

exercises.english: She has neither job offers nor a salary.
exercises.german: Sie hat weder Jobangebote noch ein Gehalt.
exercises.why: The two elements may differ in number, which weder … noch tolerates.

exercises.english: She speaks both English and French.
exercises.german: Sie spricht sowohl Englisch als auch Französisch.
exercises.why: sowohl … als auch adds two elements; the verb spricht stays in position II.

exercises.english: He is both a doctor and a teacher.
exercises.german: Er ist sowohl Arzt als auch Lehrer.
exercises.why: Two professions after sein, with the pair in the middle.

exercises.english: I have both time and money.
exercises.german: Ich habe sowohl Zeit als auch Geld.
exercises.why: The shared noun follows the whole pair, not the second element.

exercises.english: We waited both for the bus and for the train.
exercises.german: Wir warteten sowohl auf den Bus als auch auf den Zug.
exercises.why: Both prepositional phrases follow the pair; the verb warteten stays in position II.

exercises.english: The letter was both confusing and rude.
exercises.german: Der Brief war sowohl verwirrend als auch unhöflich.
exercises.why: Two predicative adjectives joined by the pair.

exercises.english: She is both intelligent and hard-working.
exercises.german: Sie ist sowohl intelligent als auch fleißig.
exercises.why: sowohl … als auch works with sein and predicative adjectives.

exercises.english: I like both coffee and tea.
exercises.german: Ich trinke sowohl Kaffee als auch Tee gern.
exercises.why: The verb trinke keeps position II; gern may follow the pair.

exercises.english: He works both in Berlin and in Vienna.
exercises.german: Er arbeitet sowohl in Berlin als auch in Wien.
exercises.why: Two prepositional phrases of one clause; the infinitive-free verb stays in position II.

exercises.english: We saw both the film and the trailer.
exercises.german: Wir haben sowohl den Film als auch den Trailer gesehen.
exercises.why: Two accusative objects; the participle gesehen stays last.

exercises.english: The problem is both financial and legal.
exercises.german: Das Problem ist sowohl finanziell als auch rechtlich.
exercises.why: Adjectives derived from nouns, uninflected after a linking verb.

exercises.english: She can both swim and dive.
exercises.german: Sie kann sowohl schwimmen als auch tauchen.
exercises.why: Modal kann in position II, then the pair, then both infinitives.

exercises.english: It was both cheap and good quality.
exercises.german: Es war sowohl billig als auch hochwertig.
exercises.why: Two predicative adjectives after war.

exercises.english: He speaks both at home and at work.
exercises.german: Er spricht sowohl zu Hause als auch bei der Arbeit.
exercises.why: The preposition is repeated for each location.

exercises.english: We would like both tea and a cake.
exercises.german: Wir hätten sowohl Tee als auch einen Kuchen gern.
exercises.why: Two accusative objects with a modal; the infinitive of haben leads.

exercises.english: She is both very tall and very slim.
exercises.german: Sie ist sowohl sehr groß als auch sehr schlank.
exercises.why: Degree adverbs sit inside each element, not between the pair.

exercises.english: I know both of them.
exercises.german: Ich kenne sowohl sie als auch ihn.
exercises.why: sowohl … als auch can join two pronouns without a repeated preposition.

exercises.english: Not only is he intelligent, but he is also hard-working.
exercises.german: Er ist nicht nur intelligent, sondern auch fleißig.
exercises.why: The comma before sondern is compulsory; the pair spans both halves of the sentence.

exercises.english: It is not only cheap but also good.
exercises.german: Es ist nicht nur billig, sondern auch hochwertig.
exercises.why: Both elements are predicative after the same verb, which stays in position II.

exercises.english: She speaks not only German but also English.
exercises.german: Sie spricht nicht nur Deutsch, sondern auch Englisch.
exercises.why: The verb spricht appears once; two languages are added.

exercises.english: He is not only a teacher but also a musician.
exercises.german: Er ist nicht nur Lehrer, sondern auch Musiker.
exercises.why: Two professions after one verb, linked by the pair.

exercises.english: I not only know him but also respect him.
exercises.german: Ich kenne ihn nicht nur, sondern ich respektiere ihn auch.
exercises.why: When the two halves have different objects, the second clause repeats the verb.

exercises.english: The course is not only theory but also practice.
exercises.german: Der Kurs ist nicht nur Theorie, sondern auch Praxis.
exercises.why: Two nouns as predicative complements after sein.

exercises.english: She not only came but also stayed.
exercises.german: Sie kam nicht nur, sondern sie blieb auch.
exercises.why: The first verb closes the first element; the second element repeats the verb for the new subject.

exercises.english: It not only rained but also snowed.
exercises.german: Es regnete nicht nur, sondern es schneite auch.
exercises.why: When the two weather predicates belong to the same subject, the second can share the subject with a new verb.

exercises.english: We have not only time but also motivation.
exercises.german: Wir haben nicht nur Zeit, sondern auch Motivation.
exercises.why: The verb haben stays in position II and governs both nouns.

exercises.english: He is not only lazy but also unfriendly.
exercises.german: Er ist nicht nur faul, sondern auch unfreundlich.
exercises.why: Two predicative adjectives with the comma before sondern.

exercises.english: The film was not only boring but also very long.
exercises.german: Der Film war nicht nur langweilig, sondern auch sehr lang.
exercises.why: Degree adverbs go inside the second element.

exercises.english: She writes not only poems but also novels.
exercises.german: Sie schreibt nicht nur Gedichte, sondern auch Romane.
exercises.why: The verb schreibt keeps position II across both objects.

exercises.english: We would like to book not only a table but also a menu.
exercises.german: Wir möchten sowohl einen Tisch als auch ein Menü buchen.
exercises.why: sowohl … als auch is the neutral alternative when both elements are simply added.

exercises.english: It was not only expensive but also disappointing.
exercises.german: Es war nicht nur teuer, sondern auch enttäuschend.
exercises.why: Two predicative adjectives after war.

exercises.english: He can not only drive but also repair cars.
exercises.german: Er kann nicht nur fahren, sondern auch Autos reparieren.
exercises.why: Modal kann in position II; each element gets its own infinitive, the second with its object.

exercises.english: She not only speaks Spanish but also teaches it.
exercises.german: Sie spricht nicht nur Spanisch, sondern unterrichtet es auch.
exercises.why: The second clause needs its own verb because the subjects of the two actions differ.

exercises.english: The results are not only good but also reproducible.
exercises.german: Die Ergebnisse sind nicht nur gut, sondern auch reproduzierbar.
exercises.why: Two predicative adjectives after sind.

exercises.english: I not only forgot my keys but also locked the door.
exercises.german: Ich vergaß nicht nur meine Schlüssel, sondern schloss auch die Tür ab.
exercises.why: The second element carries its own separable verb, whose prefix goes last.

exercises.english: I don't know either the answer or the question.
exercises.german: Ich kenne weder die Antwort noch die Frage.
exercises.why: weder … noch negates by itself; adding nicht would give a double negative.

exercises.english: He won't come either on Monday or on Tuesday.
exercises.german: Er kommt weder am Montag noch am Dienstag.
exercises.why: The negation sits in the verb, not in the connector pair.

exercises.english: Not only does she want it, she needs it too.
exercises.german: Nicht nur will sie es, sie braucht es auch.
exercises.why: With the verb first, the negated element nicht nur comes right after it.

exercises.english: I have neither the time nor the will.
exercises.german: Ich habe weder die Zeit noch den Willen.
exercises.why: weder … noch replaces a repeated nicht; both nouns keep their articles.

exercises.english: He is neither right nor entirely wrong.
exercises.german: Er hat weder ganz recht noch ganz unrecht.
exercises.why: Degree adverbs sit inside each element.

exercises.english: She has neither a car nor a bicycle.
exercises.german: Sie hat weder ein Auto noch ein Fahrrad.
exercises.why: Two accusative nouns with articles; kein would need the negated pattern instead.

exercises.english: We will not eat both fish and meat.
exercises.german: Wir werden weder Fisch noch Fleisch essen.
exercises.why: weder … noch with a future auxiliary in position II and the infinitive last.

exercises.english: Neither option is free.
exercises.german: Keine der beiden Möglichkeiten ist kostenlos.
exercises.why: With keine, the correlative takes a singular verb, unlike weder … noch.

exercises.english: He can neither read nor write.
exercises.german: Er kann weder lesen noch schreiben.
exercises.why: The modal kann is shared by both negated infinitives.

exercises.english: I don't like either the red or the blue one.
exercises.german: Ich mag weder das rote noch das blaue.
exercises.why: Adjective endings after das follow the zero-article pattern.

exercises.english: Not only is she late, she is also forgetful.
exercises.german: Nicht nur ist sie spät, sie ist auch vergesslich.
exercises.why: The fronted nicht nur takes the verb immediately after it.

exercises.english: We have not only enough but also too much.
exercises.german: Wir haben nicht nur genug, sondern auch zu viel.
exercises.why: sowohl would not fit here: the second element contrasts rather than adds, so sondern is required.

exercises.english: Both the sentence and the punctuation are wrong.
exercises.german: Sowohl der Satz als auch die Zeichensetzung sind falsch.
exercises.why: Two subjects joined by the pair take a plural verb, which comes last.

exercises.english: He neither admitted it nor denied it.
exercises.german: Er gab es weder zu, noch leugnete er es.
exercises.why: Inverted order puts the finite verb first, then the pair, then noch.

exercises.english: It is not only cheaper but also faster.
exercises.german: Es ist nicht nur billiger, sondern auch schneller.
exercises.why: Comparative adverbs live inside each element; the verb ist stays in position II.

exercises.english: Whether it rains or snows, we are going.
exercises.german: Ob es regnet oder schneit, gehen wir.
exercises.why: In a verb-first clause the connector pair sits after the subject.

exercises.english: Both options have advantages and disadvantages.
exercises.german: Beide Möglichkeiten haben sowohl Vor- als auch Nachteile.
exercises.why: sowohl … als auch with a hyphen on the elided second noun.

exercises.english: He works either in the morning or in the evening.
exercises.german: Er arbeitet entweder morgens oder abends.
exercises.why: The verb bleibt in position II; both time expressions are adverbials of one clause.

exercises.english: Neither the first nor the second answer was right.
exercises.german: Weder die erste noch die zweite Antwort war richtig.
exercises.why: Ordinal adjectives take normal endings after the articles of each element.

exercises.english: Not only the teacher but also the pupils were late.
exercises.german: Nicht nur die Lehrerin, sondern auch die Schüler waren zu spät.
exercises.why: The verb war applies to both elements and comes last.

exercises.english: Either take the bus or call me.
exercises.german: Nimm entweder den Bus oder ruf mich an.
exercises.why: Imperative with the verb first: the pair follows it, and the separable prefix an- goes last.

exercises.english: She can both cook and clean.
exercises.german: Sie kann sowohl kochen als auch putzen.
exercises.why: Modal kann in position II, then the pair, then both infinitives.

exercises.english: I have neither seen it nor heard of it.
exercises.german: Ich habe es weder gesehen noch davon gehört.
exercises.why: Two participles after one auxiliary, following the pair in the same order.

exercises.english: Not only did he apologise, he also paid.
exercises.german: Nicht nur entschuldigte er sich, er zahlte auch.
exercises.why: Inverted order: the finite verb follows the negated element, the second clause adds auch.

exercises.english: The longer you practise, the better you get.
exercises.german: Je länger du übst, desto besser wirst du.
exercises.why: je … desto with comparatives; both halves keep a comma between element and main clause.

exercises.english: The earlier you leave, the better it is.
exercises.german: Je früher du gehst, desto besser ist es.
exercises.why: The same pattern with a comparative in both elements.

exercises.english: The more you practise, the more confident you become.
exercises.german: Je mehr du übst, umso sicherer wirst du.
exercises.why: After je mehr, umso is used instead of desto.

exercises.english: The harder it is, the more necessary it becomes.
exercises.german: Je schwieriger es ist, umso notwendiger wird es.
exercises.why: umso after the first je-clause keeps the correlation strict.

exercises.english: The earlier we start, the sooner we finish.
exercises.german: Je früher wir anfangen, desto früher sind wir fertig.
exercises.why: Two temporal comparatives, same structure.

exercises.english: The more he earns, the more he spends.
exercises.german: Je mehr er verdient, desto mehr gibt er aus.
exercises.why: Two amounts compared against each other.
